maria (sec): Quick sync — we need to lock down lifecycle + access for the field_access logs we forward to SIEM. HIPAA reviewers asked for field-level retention and masking strategy.

ben (sre): Got it. Do we want tiers (hot/warm/cold/archive) or just short live + long-term?

maria (sec): Tiers. Proposal: 7d hot (full fidelity), 90d warm (masked PII), 6y archive (tokenized + KMS-wrapped). Keeps audits + e-discovery covered.

ashley (compliance): 6y aligns with our retention baseline for regulated data, yes. Need clear justification in the policy doc and a TTL enforcement plan.

noah (infra): Implementation note: SIEM (Splunk) indexes -> cold storage export to S3 using lifecycle rules. We can attach a customer-managed KMS key and rotate yearly. Example export config: ```aws s3 cp s3://redwood-siem-archive/2026/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh-1234```

audit-bot: [automated] New export job queued: export-2026-03-15T02:00Z (status: queued) :white_check_mark:

charlie (legal): Two asks: (1) confirm who can request a full-fidelity restore (forensics vs legal), (2) record the legal justification for retention in the policy doc.

maria (sec): For restores I propose: only "forensics-oncall" and "legal-requests" roles can request; approval via JIRA + 2nd approver from security. Keep restore timeboxed.

ben (sre): Access model: create scoped SIEM role 'siem_read_field_access' that excludes PHI fields by default. For restores we issue a time-limited role that logs every query. We can use OKTA session tagging + short-lived STS creds.

noah (infra): Example STS flow: create-session -> assume-role:siem-restore -> session duration 1h -> session logged to audit-bucket. We can export the query audit trail to KMS-encrypted S3.

ashley (compliance): Masking rules need to be explicit. Example: username -> hash (sha256 + salt), email -> truncated (first char + @domain removed), ip -> /24. Any PHI like patient_id must be tokenized.

maria (sec): Agreed. Also requirement: any SIEM export job must be wrapped with KMS key and MFA required on request. No plain-text PHI in transit.

ben (sre): Two operational items: (A) add a pre-export scan that flags potential PHI fields (heuristics), (B) block exports older than 6y unless legal approves. I can prototype the scan as a lambda.

charlie (legal): Good. Make legal approval explicit: JIRA ticket with reason + retention end date + requestor identity. We'll sign off on write-access to archived buckets only after review.

maria (sec): One more: we had a near-miss last month where a dev requested broad queries and got elevated access. Proposal: require "access-justification" field on the request and auto-revoke if no review within 24h.

ben (sre): Fine. I can add an enforcement webhook to the approval workflow. If not approved -> revoke.

noah (infra): Ops note: KMS key policy must include: allow:Encrypt/Decrypt for SIEM service principal + explicit principals for restore roles, deny for everyone else. We'll draft key policy.

ashley (compliance): Can we add an annual audit that samples 10 restores and verifies masking & approvals?

maria (sec): Yes. Action items: ben -> prototype pre-export PHI scan + scoped role (ETA 2w). noah -> KMS key policy draft + STS workflow (ETA 1w). ashley -> update policy wording and audit plan (ETA 1w). charlie -> provide legal approval template (ETA 3d). I'll collate into a single doc. :clipboard: 

ben (sre): ACK. I'll open a tracking ticket and link the prototype.

audit-bot: [automated] Ticket created: SIEM-9123 "field_access export lifecycle + JIT restore" assigned to ben (sre).

maria (sec): Thanks all — we'll iterate on the doc in #eng-security but will bring to the next compliance review. :thumbsup:
